edits.text: The Buyer shall pay the Seller USD 41,000,000 for the Shares. The purchase price shall be subject to adjustment based on the final working capital as of the Closing Date, on a dollar-for-dollar basis above or below an agreed target working capital amount to be finalized pre-Closing.

At Closing, the Seller shall deliver: (a) duly executed share transfer forms for all Shares; (b) share certificates (if any); (c) resignation letters from directors as reasonably requested by the Buyer; and (d) any other documents reasonably necessary to transfer good title to the Shares. The Buyer shall pay the Purchase Price (as adjusted, if applicable) at Closing.

The Seller makes the following representations and warranties as of the date of this Agreement and as of Closing:
(a) Organization and Authority. Seller is duly organized and has full power and authority to enter into this Agreement.
(b) Title to Shares. Seller is the sole legal and beneficial owner of the Shares, free and clear of all liens or encumbrances.
(c) Financial Statements. The financial statements provided to Buyer are accurate in all material respects.
(d) Litigation. To Seller's knowledge, there is no litigation pending or threatened against the Seller or the Company that would affect the Shares or the transaction.
(e) Compliance with Laws. The Company is in material compliance with applicable laws.
(f) No Undisclosed Liabilities. Except as disclosed, the Company has no material liabilities other than as reflected in the financial statements or arising in the ordinary course since the date thereof.
Each representation is qualified by Seller’s knowledge and the disclosures in the data room.
Buyer may rely on these representations and warranties, which shall survive for 18 months following Closing, except for title and authority representations, which shall survive indefinitely.

The confidentiality obligations in this Section shall extend to all transaction-related information, including but not limited to the existence, terms, negotiations, and related documentation of this Agreement. These obligations shall survive Closing or termination of this Agreement for a period of 2 years.

5. Escrow and Indemnity.
(a) Escrow. USD 2,000,000 of the Purchase Price shall be deposited in escrow for a period of 18 months to satisfy any claims for indemnification by Buyer under this Agreement.
(b) Indemnity. Seller shall indemnify Buyer for actual losses arising from a breach of Seller’s representations and warranties or pre-Closing tax liabilities, subject to: (i) an aggregate cap equal to the escrow amount, and (ii) a minimum claim threshold of USD 100,000.

Having reviewed the revised draft, our client remains concerned with valuation given the due diligence, sector trends, and certain potential liabilities. Accordingly, the Buyer’s best offer stands at USD 39,000,000, subject to final adjustments.

With respect to the new provisions:
- The target working capital mechanism must be set based on the trailing 12-month average, not by Seller.
- Escrow should cover not less than USD 4,000,000 to properly protect against credible risks. We request the indemnity cap be raised to 10% of purchase price and the minimum claim threshold reduced to USD 50,000. Buyer does not accept the full knowledge and data room carve-outs as drafted; reps must be based on Seller’s actual knowledge and only certain, identified disclosures.
- Please expand the reps to the usual full set (tax, employees, IP, anti-bribery, environmental, etc.), and confirm all disclosure schedules will be provided for our review at least 5 business days pre-closing.
- Confidentiality should recognize Buyer’s need to disclose to its affiliates, lenders, and advisors, and provide for standard compelled-disclosure exceptions.

Please provide an updated draft reflecting these changes. We remain keen to progress negotiations to a mutually beneficial outcome.

Kind regards,
Bellweather Croft LLP

probe.private_reasoning: The Seller's initial draft started with $45M and then quickly dropped to $41M following the Buyer's feedback. There is no resistance shown in the language or indications that this is a firm 'bottom line'—instead, the cover note says 'willing to move to a price of USD 41,000,000,' which signals more flexibility. Sellers often do not expose their real minimum at this stage, and the lack of comments or metadata suggesting internal communications about price supports that. Furthermore, the Seller offered a meaningful price reduction on the first counter—strongly suggesting padding remains. The tracked changes provide details that seem designed to demonstrate responsiveness and good faith, but not insistence. Based on negotiation conventions and recognizing this is only round two, the Seller's client would probably accept at least $37M, maybe lower depending on remaining deal terms and due diligence.
